A video titles itself, and those titles carry operators — a leading '~' is remove-cell, so the create never happened at all; '&', '#' and '?' truncated 'Q&A #5 what?! + more' to 'qa'. entries.title: Note the three ways a link drop used to do nothing at all
entries.note: MANUAL — note-add is additive. THREE fixes so a dropped link can never silently do nothing. (1) DRAGOVER CLAIMS ANYTHING CARRYING A LINK: it used to refuse when the source ADVERTISED the 'Files' type, which a dragged browser TAB and links out of native apps do while delivering no file at all — no preventDefault meant the drop event was never delivered and the whole gesture vanished. Real files are still handed to ImageDropDrone, decided at drop by dataTransfer.files.length, which is the only place it is knowable. (2) NO IN-FLIGHT GUARD: #busy was held across every await of the route (safety check, card read, picture fetch), so a second drop within those seconds was discarded without a trace, and any route that never settled wedged the gesture PERMANENTLY. Each drop is its own gesture now, carrying its own armId; per-cell writes already serialise on their own lock. (3) ARM BEFORE THE SAFETY CHECK: the arm sat behind an LLM safety call whose endpoint is loopback (127.0.0.1:4220) and can be absent or behind a Local Network Access prompt. The chevron now lights on release and a denied link RETRACTS it via command:disarm-resource.

(2) DEADLINES ON EVERY NETWORK STEP (deadline.ts): card read 3.5s, picture 5s, safety verdict 5s, each aborting what it abandons. A hung request is worse than a failed one — it parked the whole drop with no title, no picture and no tile. (3) THE PICTURE IS BEST-EFFORT IN THE STORE TOO: armImageBlob throwing used to take the link with it; it now degrades to the bare arm. (4) THE TRAP THAT COST A DAY: the packed store admits ONE WRITER — a second tab on the same origin comes up with opfsAvailable false and putResource throwing 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading getFileHandle)'. Every symptom of a dead drop follows. Console says it plainly: '[packed-store] unavailable — held by another tab'. NEVER open a second tab (in-app browser pane, MCP tab, Playwright against the same profile) on a hive someone is using; Playwright with its own profile is safe. entries.title: Global fit reconciles against the surface + chrome, not just window resize
entries.note: Fix: the global fit switch refit was bound only to window 'resize'. When the DRAWING SURFACE changed with no window resize (a panel reserving a column, the shell re-laying out) or when only the CHROME moved (header grows a row as a drop arms the command line, controls rail docks/undocks), nothing refit — the page kept the scale/position computed for the previous safe area, leaving content small and pushed into a corner. pixi-host already reconciled the CANVAS for this reason (resyncToHost) but only recentres the stage, so the renderer reported the new surface while the fit kept the old framing. Now a 250ms signature reconciler samples canvas box + --hc-controls-left/right + header bottom and refits only on change. Owed: a note on the fit-switch tile under behaviors describing the two non-window triggers, so the mark explains why the fit follows chrome. Manual because note-add is additive and would land twice.

entries.title: Global fit: back-nav paints land BEFORE the navigate that arms them
entries.note: Fix: arrived() was gated purely on an arm set by the window 'navigate' event. Verified event order — forward nav: navigate -> cell-count (fit runs). BACK nav (MovementService.back / history.back): cell-count, cell-count, THEN navigate. Every paint at the destination ran unarmed and bailed, so the page was NEVER refit on the way back; it kept whatever stale snapshot the viewport store held (auto-fits never persist, so that snapshot can be from any earlier moment) — the 'it shrinks when I click back' report. Now arrived() also treats an unsettled page key as an arrival (#lastSettledPageKey), so the fit is independent of event ORDER; add/remove stillness is preserved because those paint the same key already settled. Owed: a note on the fit-switch tile under behaviors recording that arrival is a LOCATION change, not an event, and why back-nav inverts the order.

entries.title: Viewport source splits GESTURE from PERSIST — 'auto-persist' added, ratchet frozen
entries.note: Sweep after the back-click fix. Root cause class: automatic code borrowing a user-gesture path. (1) source 'user' meant BOTH 'persist this' and 'the participant asked' — the latter announces viewport:fit, which the control bar uses to DISCARD a page's hand framing. Three automatic callers claimed 'user' purely to persist (auto-fit-first-add, show-cell first-visit fit, and the comments all said 'so it STICKS'): a first-tile add or first-visit render silently stripped a hand framing and the page re-fitted forever after. Added ViewportSource 'auto-persist' = persists (even through suspend) but never announces; migrated the two truly automatic callers; sequence-cycle stays 'user' (it follows an "a" keypress). (2) Mirror image: zoomByFactor/zoomToScale/animateToScale unconditionally emitted viewport:manual, which MARKS a page hand-framed — so the tutorial zoom LESSON permanently excluded whatever page it ran on from global fit. Added a source param defaulting to 'user'; tutorial passes 'auto'. Also fixed controls-bar passing an undeclared third arg 'controls-bar' that would now read as a source and demote the magnifier buttons. (3) pixi-host now emits render:surface-resized from resyncToHost — the missing 'the canvas changed size without a window resize' signal; center-slot-tracker consumed it (its scores were ranking slots against a dead viewport after a panel opened). Guard: doctrine.spec.ts ratchet 'viewport source user means a GESTURE' with a 4-entry allowlist, verified to FAIL when the regression is reintroduced. Owed: a note on the fit-switch tile recording the two-question source model (persist vs gesture) and why marks/mode changes must never ride a gesture path.

entries.title: Note the hyperlink-vs-image drop arbitration on the link-drop tile
entries.note: MANUAL — note-add is additive. THE bug behind 'no text, no link, file icon at the top': dragging a video off the YouTube page packages an IMAGE FILE and the URL in one drag. ImageDropDrone registered first and claimed any drop with files, so the gesture minted a mute picture tile — no name, no link — and LinkDropWorker never saw it (its own guard bailed on files.length). Arbitration is now BY CONTENT and order-independent, decided identically on both sides via extractDroppedUrl (link-drop-destination.ts): a drop carrying a URL that is NOT itself an image is a HYPERLINK — the link path claims it and the dragged file becomes the tile's picture (beats fetching); no URL, or a URL that IS the image (a bare drag), stays with the image path. entries.title: Installer names every artifact — the class name declares the role, never the signature
entries.note: MANUAL — note-add is additive. THE BUG: ~130 of 2039 bee sigs rendered their SIGNATURE as their name in the installer, and (because the failure path also returns kind 'bee') the generic hexagon instead of their own glyph. Two populations, one cause: both the build-time doc extractor (hypercomb-essentials/scripts/build-module.ts extractBeeDoc) and the installer's runtime fallback (diamond-core-processor tree-resolver.service.ts) recognised an artifact ONLY by 'export class X extends QueenBee|Worker|Drone|Bee'. A *Drone extending EventTarget (47 files) and a *QueenBee extending nothing at all (85 files) matched neither, so no doc was written and no name could be recovered. THE RULE NOW: the class NAME declares the role; the base class only confirms it. Four tiers, weakest last — base class, class name suffix, then the FILE name (layer-committer.drone.ts is a drone even though LayerCommitter says nothing); a *.service.ts ships as a bee sig too, so it is named as one. Orthogonal to all three: a class whose name matches the file's own stem outranks one that does not, because a bundle INLINES its helpers and without it the first class wins — layer-committer.drone.ts was named after its internal CommitMachine, and later after the inlined HistoryService. ALSO: the two runtime detectors (#detectBeeInfo and #detectBeeInfoLocal) each carried their own copy of the regex and had drifted; they now share ONE #scanBundle. TRAP THAT COST AN HOUR: SigInfoCache PERSISTS derivations to localStorage['dcp.sigInfo'] — a wrong name survives every reload and rebuild, so verifying a naming change means clearing that key first, not just reloading. NEW: every bee row carries sourcePath, read off the bundle's first-line esbuild comment (nothing read it before) — shown as the crumb when there is no lineage and as the row's title, and searchable, so a path pasted from the editor finds its row. Owed under behaviors: a part tile for each of build-module.ts extractBeeDoc, tree-resolver #scanBundle, and sig-info-cache.ts, with notes carrying the four-tier rule and the localStorage trap. SAME PASS also shipped the installer's SEARCH BOX (filter-as-you-type over name + className + sourcePath, auto-expanding to reveal matches) and made resolved trees land COLLAPSED at the root level (#openRootItems no longer opens every root — a resolved tree can carry hundreds of leaves). REBUILT + VERIFIED 2026-08-25: essentials rebuilt (root 67206707bdcb, v57 'main'), 117/117 bee sigs in the package now carry a doc — zero without. Two derived caches had to be version-stamped before either fix could take effect, and that is the transferable lesson: a cache keyed by a SIGNATURE is not self-invalidating, because the bytes are immutable but the deriving CODE is not. (a) SigInfoCache now carries DERIVATION_VERSION and drops the record whole on mismatch — without it a wrong name persisted in localStorage['dcp.sigInfo'] survives every reload and rebuild, so the fix runs and the cache answers first. (b) build-module's docCache is keyed by SOURCE CONTENT, so editing the EXTRACTOR invalidated nothing — 333 files sat cached as doc:null; BuildCache.version 5→6 is what makes an extractor change take effect at all. Also owed: a part tile for sig-info-cache.ts carrying the (signature, derivation version) rule.

entries.title: Done LEAVES; adopt/save/discard COMMIT; one restore point instead of two
entries.note: Shipped with no mirror pass (no bridge this session). (1) The embedded installer's bottom bar is ONE button, 'done', and Done only LEAVES — no save, no install, so it can never fail and strand the participant (a restore point that would not save used to hold the panel open and lock the hexagons out). (2) ALL THREE INSTALLER VERBS COMMIT: adopt (install+enable), save (installed but off) and discard (uninstall) each post dcp:confirm to the parent AFTER their registry snapshot, which reaches apply() -> actions:available, still the sole authorization signal for the hive fold and the shell resync. One helper, #signalCommit, and the uninstall path signals from removeDomain so the row's DISCARD and the domain header's x are the same act. Adopt is pressable on an already-adopted package (the commit is about the STATE — a bee flipped on inside a package — not the package). removeDomain now AWAITS its sigbag removals and pushes a recomputed registry before signalling; it used to fire and forget and never told the hive at all. (3) SIMPLIFICATION: the portal chrome no longer takes a hive restore point of its own. There were TWO snapshots of the same hive on one accept — the portal's (fail-CLOSED, always, blocking) and SwarmAdoptDrone's pre-fold checkpoint (fail-OPEN, only on a real diff, self-named) — and the drone's ran precisely when the portal's did not. The portal's is deleted; the typed name now rides in the actions:available detail (it was already being sent and ignored) and names the drone's checkpoint. A package-only accept takes no hive seal — its way back is the installer's own revision history. (4) The installer's tree lands with every ROOT item expanded. Files: hypercomb-shared/ui/portal/portal-overlay.component.{html,ts,scss}, diamond-core-processor/src/app/home/home.component.ts, hypercomb-essentials/src/diamondcoreprocessor.com/sharing/swarm-adopt.drone.ts (+ its checkpoint spec), hypercomb-web/src/main.ts (comments). Owed under behaviors: the installer/portal cards must say Done is an EXIT, the three verbs are the accept, and there is ONE restore point per accept, taken by the fold.

entries.title: A picture is a reference - paste or drop one into a question and the responder opens it
entries.note: Jaime 2026-08-24, approved bridge tier. The chat window takes an IMAGE now: paste into the composer or drop on the shelf. The bytes go to the hive through Store.putResource - content in, signature out, so the same screenshot pasted twice is stored once (verified: the shelf refuses the duplicate because the sig is identical). The shelf chip wears the picture itself as its mark, its file name, and its WEIGHT where a tile's branch would be (chat.reference.picture, all 14 catalogs; chat.reference.empty now names the picture too). The ask carries {kind:'<media type>', sig, label} - the MEDIA TYPE is the kind, so one field says both 'this is a picture' and 'this is how to open it'; llm.queen already passes references through untouched. The responder half already existed: the bridge's get-resource serves any resource base64, so a session writes the bytes to a file and READS it - .claude/skills/bridge-listen/SKILL.md now says so, before replying, because answering about a picture you did not look at is guessing. entries.title: A grinding chat must not take the main thread from the bees
entries.note: Jaime 2026-08-25: 'we have to make sure the bees are working while the chat sessions are grinding - as long as there is a connection.' Found: the rail re-walked the ENTIRE threads pool on every landing turn (and briefly TWICE per turn, from the hive row's own list) - with 14 conversations that is 14 bucket reads + 14 title resource reads per reply, on the same main thread the processor pulses on, at exactly the moment a session is delivering replies in a burst. Built: chat-thread.listRailConversations (ONE walk, a chat about no tile filed at HIVE_PATH) replaces the two lists; chat-thread.readConversationSummary reads ONE bucket by its own sha256 name; the rail's chat:threads-changed handler now merges the NAMED conversation and coalesces a burst (CHAT_SETTLE_MS 180) into one repaint, falling back to the walk when a change names no thread or more than CHAT_MERGE_CAP=12 threads changed at once. Measured with scripts/drive-chat-grind-cost.cjs on dev 4450: a burst of 8 replies = 8 pool walks -> 0 walks + 8 bucket opens. Also fixed on the way: CSS.escape is absent in jsdom (and older webviews) and every row lookup used it - now a dataset walk, which cannot be broken by a character in a tile's name either; entering a chat re-renders the level, so the keyboard's focus is put back on the row it was standing on; walking into a level with the keyboard lands on the first TILE, not the hive row above them. Verified: agent-tiles-rail.spec + doctrine 130 green, drive-chat-lines-under-tile 13 green. NOT covered: the optimize phase is idle+2s-timeout scheduled (never starved outright) and the bridge's quiet-landing window already coalesces repaints - both were read, neither needed changing. entries.title: Mirror the DCP client-registry rework — the resting list is ONE row, the install you are on
Archive a conversation — put away, not thrown away
entries.note: One themed card on the behaviors mirror. ARCHIVE: delete was the only thing you could do with a conversation you were finished with, and it is the wrong verb — you are done needing the thread, not done having said it. The flag is a marker FILE IN THE THREAD'S OWN BUCKET (sign('threads') pool), never an index and never localStorage: the bucket already describes itself, and 'I am finished with this' is a fact about the thread, not about this device, so it travels and survives storage being cleared. Named by a constant, not by content hash, because unlike a turn it is mutable. The list still REPORTS an archived thread — hiding it is the surface's job; a list that dropped it would leave no way back. An archived thread is never what a window resumes into, and its turns no longer count toward its tile's row mark. One control both directions in the rail's fold and in the window's flat list, behind an 'Archived (n)' disclosure. Tiles: chat-thread.ts (setConversationArchived, ARCHIVE_MARKER, BucketRead, foldTileConversations), agent-tiles-rail.ts, chat-window.component.{ts,html,scss}, drive-chat-archive.cjs, chat-thread-shape.spec.ts.

entries.title: Archive the chat you are IN — the bar icon
entries.note: Extends the chat-archive card. The per-row control in the fold acts on a conversation you are POINTING at; this one acts on the one you are READING, which is the common case. It sits in the bar above the transcript, left of the + with a hairline rule between them, and NEITHER icon wears a border — two outlined boxes at the end of a row holding a name read as a toolbar bolted onto a title; the rule says they are different kinds of act without drawing boxes. Filing from here MOVES ON to the next live thread (or a fresh chat when that was the last) — the one place staying put would be wrong, because a press that files the thread and leaves it on screen looks like a press that did nothing. Un-filing stays put. setConversationArchived now announces chat:threads-changed itself, so every surface listing the thread hears it. Tiles: chat-window.component.{ts,html,scss} (.chat-put, .chat-bar-split, archiveCurrent, activeArchived), chat-thread.ts.

entries.title: Point and click a tile onto the request
entries.note: Extends the chat-peek card. Folding the window away lets you FIND the tiles a request should carry; this is the affordance for putting them ON the shelf, because the one gesture the canvas already owns (drag) is a PAN. A tile icon appears on every hexagon while the window is folded away and is unregistered when it comes back — an add-to-the-request button on a surface with no request behind it does nothing, and actionsForTile also feeds the close-up and the brief. WHY AN ICON NOT A DRAG HANDLE: a pan-locked drag costs a MODE paid per tile (press, hold, cross, release), and gathering context is a repeated discrete act — the cheap repeatable gesture wins. WHY NOT CTRL-CLICK: the chord already means selection/wand on a hexagon. Same control both directions — a tile already on the shelf wears the icon LIT (steel, the chat window's colour) and pressing it takes the tile off. The SIGNATURE is resolved through levelRoster, the list the rail/notes/command line all read, so the sig matches what a drag off the rail would carry. Tiles: chat-context-action.drone.ts (NEW), chat-window.component.ts (chat:peek, chat:add-context, toggleContext), side-effects.ts, drive-chat-context-icon.cjs.

entries.title: Common Tongue: the words you lead with are offered back, and complete as plain TEXT
entries.note: Extends the spoken-habits card on the behaviors mirror. Habits already answered once the line had become a sentence ('open ' -> 'open providers'); nothing answered BEFORE the first space, so a participant who could not remember the whole phrasing got no help starting it. Now the discovered lead-ins themselves are rows: 'op' offers 'open', 'sh' offers 'show'. THE ROW IS A WORD, NOT A COMMAND - accepting it writes the word and a SPACE and runs nothing, and that space is load-bearing twice: it turns phrasings() on so the ending arrives on the next keystroke, and #completeOnEnter reads a trailing space as 'your ending goes here' so Enter completes instead of firing. STRICTLY ADDITIVE: the census speaks first and a word a behaviour already spells IS that behaviour's row (deduped, and the census wins the description and the Shift+Delete guard). Never on a blank line - Ctrl+Space asks for the catalogue and filler is not part of it. Shift+Delete on a word forgets it whole, endings included, because the word is only on offer because those phrasings exist. Part tiles 1:1: spoken-habits.ts (leadInCompletions + LeadInCompletion), command-line.component.ts (#learnedLeadIns, the suggestions append, the text-accept branch, the prune guard, slashDescriptionMap 'yours - a word - leads into <command>'), spoken-habits.spec.ts.
